title: Validate stale model-proxy PID state before signaling any process or process group
description:
## Finding

A stale/corrupt stored `u32` PID is cast to `i32`; extreme values can become negative (including process-group or broad kill semantics), and a reused PID can target an unrelated process.

## Evidence at audited commit

`crates/thegn-host/src/model_proxy_daemon.rs:124` and `crates/thegn-host/src/platform/unix.rs:113,128`.

## Implementation constraints

Treat PID files as untrusted state. Bind them to process identity/start time or an authenticated control channel. Never signal zero, negative, out-of-range, or unverified reused identifiers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PID parsing rejects zero and values above the platform's safe positive range before conversion.
- [ ] Cleanup proves the target is the expected proxy instance before TERM/KILL.
- [ ] PID reuse and stale-file cases leave unrelated processes untouched.
- [ ] Process-group signaling is explicit and only used for a group created/owned by the supervisor.
- [ ] Tests exercise `u32::MAX`, negative-cast equivalents, PID reuse, malformed state, and vanished processes.
